constituency = a district whose voters elect a representative
member of parliament = a person elected to sit in parliament
upper house = the second chamber of a parliament, such as a senate
lower house = the main elected chamber of a parliament
municipality = a town or district with its own local government
councillor = an elected member of a local council
bureaucracy = a system of administration with many official rules and procedures
red tape = official rules that seem unnecessary and delay action
watchdog organisation = a body that monitors institutions and reports abuse
public administration = the organisation and work of government offices and services
checks and balances = rules that stop any one branch of government becoming too powerful
act of parliament = a law that has been passed by parliament and come into force
electorate = all the people who are entitled to vote
turnout = the percentage of eligible voters who actually vote
coalition = an alliance of parties that govern together
referendum = a nationwide vote in which citizens decide a specific question
lobbying = trying to influence politicians and officials on behalf of a group
left-wing = supporting greater social equality and a larger role for the state
right-wing = supporting tradition, lower taxes or a smaller role for the state
centre-ground = moderate political positions between left and right
